questions.question: In Python, an if statement requires a colon (:) at the end of its header line.
The code snippet 'if x = 10:\n    print("Yes")' is a valid if statement in Python.
Python's if statements cannot combine multiple conditions with logical operators like 'and' or 'or'.
An if statement in Python can include an else clause to execute code when the condition is false.
Python supports inline if statements using a ternary operator, for example: 'result = "Yes" if condition else "No"'.
In an if-elif chain, all conditions are evaluated even after a true condition is encountered.
When using nested if statements in Python, the inner if is executed only when its outer if condition is True.
Within an if statement, Python allows the use of the 'in' operator to perform membership tests, such as 'if item in collection:'.
The expressions 'if not x is None:' and 'if x is not None:' are equivalent in Python.
In nested if statements, if an inner if statement lacks an else clause, Python automatically provides an else block that returns None.
